newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Western asks for jump in gas cost rate.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Western asks for jump in gas cost rate.

text.p: Alberta utility Canadian Western Natural Gas, a unit of ATCO Ltd, said on Thursday it applied to the province's regulator for an interim increase in the gas cost recovery rate, or cost paid for gas supply.
CWNG said greater demand for natural gas across North America and colder-than-normal temperatures in Alberta late last year and early this year resulted in rapidly increasing gas market prices.

The company said the interim increase would bring the rate to C$2.789 per gigajoule, which would be in effect from the date of a Alberta Energy and Utilities Board decision until March 31, 1997. The current rate is C$1.374 per GJ.
With the new winter rate, a typical Canadian Western residential customer using 150 GJ a year would pay about C$81 more for natural gas service in 1997, it said.
CNWG said the interim increase would not affect its 1997 summer gas cost recovery rate set at C$1.274 per GJ, effective April 1 to October 31.
"No application for an increase in the summer rate is currently planned, although Canadian Western will continue to monitor natural gas market prices closely," it said.
